messages:
infra-monitor: ALERT: hosted-api-usw2 p99 spike detected 03:12-03:18 UTC. p99=980ms, p95=420ms, frontend queue depth >80% on region cluster. Investigate.
anya: seeing it too on the per-route dashboard. spikes align with a traffic bump starting ~03:10. started `pprof` on two affected pods.
jason: any recent deploys around 02:50-03:00?
linda: rolled a kernel-selector tweak at 02:56 (PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/842). small heuristic change to prefer aux kernels for long-ish sequences.
mohit: hold—don't revert yet. my initial sampling shows increased KV-cache miss rate and reduced batch coalescing. logs: 
```
perf: avg_batch_size=6.1 -> 3.2
kvcache: miss_rate=0.14 -> 0.26 (+12% absolute)
kernelselector: fallback_count(aux)=+48%
```
priya: correlation with Tenant-42 sudden short-turn chats (many < 60 tokens). lots of small requests could reduce coalescing and force kernel fallback. noisy tenant?
sre-oncall: added tenant-level burst cap for Tenant-42 and bumped per-route rate limit from 500rps->450rps as a quick throttle. also cordoned 2 hot nodes for investigation.
deploy-bot: revert pipeline queued for `kernelselector` config (canary 10%). (deployer: linda)
anya: pprof flame shows hotspots in `kv_cache::lookup` and `batch_coalesce::coalesce_wait` with a long tail in `aux_kernel::dispatch`. stack snippets show waiting on `coalesce_timer` more often.
mohit: bisect points to the tokenizer change in abc123 that caused sequence length estimation to round up when messages contain trailing newlines -> selector thinks sequences are longer, picks aux kernel which has worse throughput at short sequences. I pinned the bisect: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/commit/abc123.
jason: so root cause chain: tenant pattern (short chats) -> sampler/coalesce produces more small batches -> tokenizer length rounding -> kernelselector picks aux -> aux has higher latency -> queues climb -> p99 spikes. correct?
mohit: yes, that's the chain. plus kvcache priming thrash when aux kernel changes memory usage pattern.
priya: mitigation options: 1) rollback tokenizer rounding (low-level commit), 2) force kernelselector config to bias primary kernel for sequences < 128, 3) tune sampler to aggressively coalesce short requests for 10s. propose doing 2 + 3 as immediate.
linda: pushed config to canary (group=10%) with `selector_bias=primary_for_short` and `coalesce_threshold=45ms`. deploy-bot applied at 03:32.
deploy-bot: deployed config sha=def456 to canary group (10%) in us-west-2.
infra-monitor: Canary metrics: canary p99 dropped to 270ms within 4m of deploy; overall region trending down but still a tail at hot-shards ~600ms. queue depth reduced on canary nodes.
mohit: I also evicted top 3 hot KV shards from noisy nodes to redistribute load. eviction logs: `kvcache.evict shard=shard-17 reason=hot_shard`
priya: I'll open a support ticket for Tenant-42 and email their SRE to ask for rate smoothing. Also scheduling a cooldown window 04:00-04:30 to observe residual tail.
jason: I'll own the rollback PR if canary doesn't hold. who is owning long-term fixes?
anya: I'll follow up on the tokenizer fix and unit tests for token-length heuristics. mohit will follow kernel selector improvements. make two tickets: RUNTIME-1912 (tokenizer), RUNTIME-1913 (selector+sampler).
sre-oncall: thanks. next steps: monitor p95/p99 for 30m, validate canary -> stage -> prod rollout if stable. escalate if p99 > 500ms persists.
linda: noted. added postmortem stub: https://goto.redwood/incidents/2026-03-18-runtime-latency-lattice (will fill details).
deploy-bot: rollback not needed yet; canary healthy.
anya: marking as investigating -> mitigated for now. will confirm after cooldown window. :white_check_mark:
